sentences.text: This annex specifies the matching mechanisms that may be used in TTCN-3 templates (and only in templates).
Specific values are the basic matching mechanism of TTCN-3 templates.
Specific values in templates are expressions which do not contain any matching mechanisms or wildcards.

Unless otherwise specified, a template field matches the corresponding field value if, and only if, the field value has exactly the same value as the value to which the expression in the template evaluates.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5.
The following matching mechanisms may be used in place of explicit values.
A template list denotes a list of acceptable values.
It can be used for values of all types.
A template list may contain values, templates obeying the template (present) restriction (see clause 15.8), and members added by all from clauses.
An all from clause comprises all elements of an existing record of or set of template into the template list.

A template field that uses a template list matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value matches any one of the values or templates in the template list, after resolving all all from clauses.
Each value or template in the template list shall be of the type declared for the template field in which this mechanism is used.
a) The type of the template list and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.
b) The template in the all from clause shall be either a specific value or combined template.
Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.
c) Individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to any of the following matching mechanisms: AnyElementsOrNone, permutation.
d) Each value or template in the template list shall be of the type declared for the template field in which this mechanism is used.
e) Templates in the template list shall obey the template (present) restriction (see clause 15.8).
EXAMPLE 1:

template MyMessageType mw_myTemplate:= 
  { 
     field1 := (2,4,6),   // list of integer values 
     field2 := ("String1", "String2"), // list of charstring values 
     :
     :
  }

The keyword complement denotes a list of values that will not be accepted as values (i.e. it is the complement of a template list).
It can be used on all values of all types.
A complemented value list may also contain templates obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).
A template field that uses complement matches the corresponding field if and only if the corresponding field's value does not match any of the values or templates listed in the template list.
The template list may be a single value, of course.
Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of an existing record of or set of template into a complement template list using an all from clause.
a) The type of the complemented template list and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.
b) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a specific value or combined template.
Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.
c) Individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to any of the following matching mechanisms: AnyElementsOrNone, permutation.
d) Each value or template in the list shall be of the type declared for the template field in which the complement is used.
e) The complement of a template list shall not match omit.
f) Templates in the complement of a template list shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

The matching symbol "?" (AnyValue) matches any value of the specified type.
It can be used on values of all types.
A template field that uses the any value mechanism matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field evaluates to a single element of the specified type.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5.

template MyMessageType mw_myTemplate:=
  { 
     field1 := ?, // will match any integer 
     field2 := ?, // will match any non-empty charstring value 
     field3 := ?, // will match true or false 
     field4 := ?    // will match any sequence of integers 
  }
The matching symbol "*" (AnyValueOrNone) is used to indicate that any valid value and the omission of the given optional field are acceptable.
It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or
record templates or to a value associated with a key of a map template.
A record or set template field that uses this symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, either the field evaluates to any element of the specified type, or if the field is absent.

A map template key that uses this symbol instead of an associated value matches the corresponding key if, and only if, either the corresponding key is present and its associated value evaluates to any value of the specified type, or if the corresponding key is absent.
a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.
b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.
Ranges indicate a bounded range of acceptable values, including or excluding the boundaries.
A template field that uses a range matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value is equal to one of the values in the range.
a) When used for values of integer or float types (and integer or float subtypes), a boundary value shall be either:
1) infinity or -infinity;
2) an expression that evaluates to a specific integer or float value.
b) The lower boundary shall be put on the left side of the range, the upper boundary at the right side.
The lower boundary shall be less than the upper boundary.

c) When used in templates or template fields of charstring or universal charstring types, the boundaries shall evaluate to valid character positions according to the coded character set table(s) of the type (e.g. the given position shall not be empty).
d) Empty positions between the lower and the upper boundaries are not considered to be valid values of the specified range.
_SuperSet is denoted by the keyword superset.
SuperSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values_ contains at least all of the elements defined within the SuperSet, and may contain more.

The successful match shall be produced only if there exists such a one-to-one mapping from the SuperSet elements to the elements of the set of values where each SuperSet element matches the element of set of values it is mapped to.

The SuperSet matching mechanism may contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8) and matching mechanisms with the restrictions given below.
However, the length matching attribute may be attached to the _SuperSet itself._

NOTE: The SuperSet matching mechanism imposes an implicit length restriction on the matched set of values, i.e. the set of values contains at least as many elements as the SuperSet template in order to produce a successful match.
Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into _SuperSets using an all from clause._
a) _SuperSet is an operation for matching that shall be used only on values of set of types._ b) Individual members of the SuperSet's argument shall be of the type replicated by the set of.
c) The member type of the set of associated with the SuperSet template and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.
d) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a specific value or combined template.
Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.

e) The individual members of the SuperSet's argument and the elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not be the matching mechanisms omit, SuperSet, SubSet and the matching attributes (length restriction and ifpresent).

In addition, the individual members shall not resolve to AnyValueOrNone and individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to _AnyElementsOrNone or permutation._ f) If the length matching attribute is attached to the SuperSet, the minimal length allowed by the length attribute shall not be less than the number of the elements in the SuperSet.
g) Templates in SuperSet's argument shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

_SubSet is denoted by the keyword subset.
SubSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values contains_ only elements defined within the SubSet, and may contain less.

The successful match shall be produced only if there exists such a one-to-one mapping from the elements of the set of values to the SubSet elements where each element of the set of values is matched by the SubSet element it is mapped to.

The SubSet matching mechanism may contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8) and matching mechanisms with the restrictions given below.
However, the length matching attribute may be attached to the SubSet itself.

The SubSet matching mechanism imposes an implicit length restriction on the matched set of values: the set of values shall contain at most as many elements as the SubSet template in order to produce a successful match.
Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into _SubSets using an all from clause._
a) _SubSet is an operation for matching that can be used only on values of set of types._ b) Individual members of the SubSet's argument shall be of the type replicated by the set of.
c) The member type of the set of type associated with the SubSet and the member type of the template in the allfrom clause shall be compatible.
d) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a matching mechanism or combined template.
Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.

e) The individual members of the SubSet's argument and the elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not be the matching mechanisms omit, SuperSet, SubSet and the matching attributes (length restriction and ifpresent).
In addition, individual members shall not resolve to AnyValueOrNone and individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
f) If the length matching attribute is attached to the SubSet, the maximum length allowed by the length attribute shall not exceed the number of the elements in the SubSet.
g) Templates in SubSet's argument shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

The keyword omit denotes that an optional field of a record or set or a specific key within a map shall be absent.
If used as a matching mechanism, it matches an optional field or a map key if and only if it is absent.
a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.
b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.
The matching symbol MatchDecodedContent `decmatch is used for checking encoded payload fields.
The matching` symbol is composed of the decmatch keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance called decoding target.

A template field that uses this symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field can be successfully decoded as an instance of the same type as the decoding target and if the decoded instance can be successfully matched by the decoding target.

The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).
a) It can be assigned to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.
b) The decoding target can be a template of any data type.

c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).
Any other value shall cause an error.
d) If the template field is of charstring type or is of universal charstring type and the encoding format is missing, the default value "UTF-8" shall be used.
NOTE: The model of the behaviour of this implicit decoding is the following.

At first, hexstring and octetstring values are implicitly converted to a bitstring value using the predefined hex2bit and oct2bit functions (specified in clauses C.1.18 and C.1.22) and charstring values are implicitly converted to universal charstring values.
Prior to decoding, the bitstring and universal charstring values are stored into a temporary anonymous variable.
Decoding is then performed by implicitly calling the predefined decvalue function (specified in clause C.5.2) for bitstring values and decvalue_unichar function for universal charstring values.
The anonymous variable containing the encoded value is passed as the first parameter to the function, the second parameter contains another temporary variable called decoded instance.
The decoded instance is of the same type as the decoding target.
If the optional encoding format parameter is present, it is passed as the third parameter to the decvalue_unichar function.
Decoding is successful only if the decoding function returns 0 and the first parameter contains an empty string (i.e. the whole encoded value has been successfully decoded).
The matching mechanism will generate an unsuccessful match if decoding hasn't succeeded.
To match an enumerated value with an associated value list in its definition, the enumerated value name shall be referenced followed by a non-empty list of integer templates in parenthesis.
The template matches only those enumerated values of the same name where the associated integer values is matched by at least one of the integer templates.
The following matching mechanisms may be used inside explicit values of strings, records of, sets of, arrays or maps.
The template that contains a matching mechanism inside a value is called a combined template.

The matching symbol "?" (AnyElement) is used to indicate that it replaces single elements of a string (except character strings, see table 4 for the lengths of the units being matched by "?" in a string), a record of, a set of or an array.
a) It shall be used only within values of string types, record of types, set of types and arrays.

template MyMessageType mw_myTemplate:=
  { :
     field2 := "abcxyz", 
     field3 := '10???'B,  // where each "?" may either be 0 or 1 
     field4 := {1, ?, 3}  // where ? may be any integer value 
  }
NOTE: The "?" in field4 can be interpreted as AnyValue as an integer value, or AnyElement inside a record of, set of or array.
Since both interpretations lead to the same match no problem arises.
If it is required to express the "?" wildcard in character strings it shall be done using character patterns (see clause B.1.5).
For example: "abcdxyz", "abccxyz", "abcxxyz" etc. will all match pattern "abc?xyz".
However, "abcxyz", "abcdefxyz", etc. will not.
The matching symbol "*" (AnyElementsOrNone) is used to indicate that it replaces none or any number of consecutive elements of a string (except character strings), a record of, a set of or an array.
The "*" symbol matches the longest sequence of elements possible, according to the pattern as specified by the symbols surrounding the "*".
_AnyElementsOrNone is also used in templates of a map type where it replaces none or any number of elements whose_ keys are not present in the map template.
If a "*" appears at the highest level inside a binary string, a record of, set of or array, it shall be interpreted as _AnyElementsOrNone._
NOTE: This rule prevents the otherwise possible interpretation of "*" as AnyValueOrNone that replaces an element inside a binary string, record of, set of or array.
a) It shall be used only within values of binary string types, record of types, set of, map types and arrays and inside the permutation matching mechanism.
If it is required to expressed the "*" wildcard in character strings it shall be done using character patterns (see clause B.1.5).
For example: "abcxyz", "abcdefxyz" "abcabcxyz" etc. will all match pattern "abc*xyz".
_Permutation is an operation for matching that shall be used only on values of record of and array types._ _Permutation is denoted by the keyword permutation.
Permutation elements shall obey the restrictions given below._

A permutation without AnyElementsOrNone in place of a single record of element means that any series of elements is acceptable provided that there is a one to one mapping between elements in the record of and in the permutation list such that each element matches its corresponding element in the permutation list.
_AnyElementsOrNone used inside permutation (directly or via reference) replaces none or any number of elements_ within the segment of the record of value matched by permutation.
The permutation matching is successful, if a subset of the elements in the record of matches the permutation list without the AnyElementsOrNone.
If both permutation and _AnyElementsOrNone are used in a record of template, they shall be evaluated jointly._

NOTE 1: _AnyElementsOrNone used inside permutation has a different effect as AnyElementsOrNone used in_ conjunction with permutation as in the latter AnyElementsOrNone replaces consecutive elements only.
For example, {permutation(1,2,*)} is equivalent to ({*,1,*,2,*},{*,2,*,1,*}), while {permutation(1,2),*} is equivalent to ({1,2,*},{2,1,*}).

NOTE 2: When AnyElementsOrNone is inside a permutation, a length attribute may be applied to _AnyElementsOrNone to restrict the number of elements matched by AnyElementsOrNone (see also_ clause B.1.4.1).
Besides specifying all individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into permutations using an all from clause.
a) Each individual member listed in the permutation shall be of the type replicated by the record of or array type.
b) The member type of the permutation and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.
c) The template referenced in the all from clause shall resolve either into specific value (see clause B.1.1) or combined template.
The combined template shall not contain permutations.
d) Void.
e) Templates except AnyElementsOrNone listed in the permutation shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

The following attributes may be associated with matching mechanisms.
The length restriction attribute is used to restrict the length of string values matching the template or the number of elements in a set `of, record` `of or array structure.`
It can also be used in conjunction with the ifpresent matching attribute.
The syntax for length can be found in clause 6.2.3.
NOTE: When the length attribute is used with a template list, elements of the list may be disabled by the attribute.
The units of length are to be interpreted according to table 4 in the main body of the present document in the case of string values.
For set of, `record of types and arrays the unit of length is the replicated type.`
A template field that uses length as an attribute of a symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field matches both the symbol and its associated attribute.
The length attribute matches if the length of the field is greater than or equal to the specified lower bound and less than or equal to the upper bound.
In the case of a single length value the length attribute matches only if the length of the received field is exactly the specified value.
It is allowed to use a length restriction in conjunction with the special value omit, however in this case the length attribute has no effect (i.e. with omit it is redundant).
With AnyValueOrNone and ifpresent it places a restriction on the value, if any.
If a length restriction is added to an AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism, it constrains the number of elements matched by this matching mechanism.
The minimum and maximum number of elements matched by the _AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism is equal to the lower bound and upper bound of the length restriction._

a) The length restriction shall be used only as an attribute of the following matching mechanisms: specific value, combined template, template list, complemented template list, AnyValue, AnyValueOrNone, AnyElement, _AnyElementsOrNone, superset, subset, and pattern._ b) It shall not be used directly with templates and template fields produced by concatenation (see clause 15.11).
If the length of a template or template field produced by concatenation is wished to be restricted, the concatenation shall be enclosed into a pair of parentheses.
c) The boundaries of the length restriction shall be denoted by expressions which resolve to specific non-negative integer values.
Alternatively, the keyword infinity can be used as a value for the upper boundary in order to indicate that there is no upper limit of length.
d) The length specifications for the template shall not conflict with the length for restrictions (if any) of the corresponding type.

e) When both the complement and the length restriction matching mechanisms are used for a template or template field, restrictions implied by them shall apply to the template or template field independently.
The ifpresent indicates that a match may be made if an optional field of a record or set or a key of a map is present (i.e. not omitted).

A template field of a record or set type that uses ifpresent matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field matches according to the associated matching mechanism, or if the field is absent.

A map template key that uses the ifpresent indicator in the value associated with it matches the corresponding key if, and only if, either the corresponding key is present and its value matches according to the associated matching mechanism, or if the corresponding key is absent.

a) This IfPresent indicator shall be used only for matching mechanisms in templates of any type as a whole or for optional fields of set or record templates or for values associated with keys of map templates.
b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.
NOTE: _AnyValueOrNone has exactly the same meaning as ? ifpresent._
Character patterns can be used in templates to define the format of a required character string to be received.
Character patterns can be used to match charstring and `universal charstring values.

In addition to literal characters,` character patterns allow the use of meta-characters (e.g. ? and * within a character pattern means matching any character and any number of any character respectively).
EXAMPLE 1:
template charstring mw_myTemplate:= pattern "ab??xyz*0";

This template will match any character string that consists of the characters "ab", followed by any two characters, followed by the characters "xyz", followed by any number of any characters (including any number of "0"-s) before the closing character "0".
If it is required to interpret any metacharacter literally it shall be preceded with the metacharacter "\".
EXAMPLE 2:
template charstring mw_myTemplate:= pattern "ab?\?xyz*";
This template would match any character string which consists of the characters "ab", followed by any character, followed by the characters "?xyz", followed by any number of any characters.
The list of meta characters for TTCN-3 patterns is shown in table B.1.
Metacharacters shall not contain whitespaces except a whitespace preceded by a newline character before or inside a set expression.
Table B.1: List of TTCN-3 pattern metacharacters
Metacharacter: ?; Description: Match any character (see notes 1 and 2)
Metacharacter: *; Description: Match any character zero or more times; shall match the longest possible number of characters (see example 1 above) (see notes 1 and 2)

Metacharacter: \; Indexing: Including the following character; Description: Cause the following metacharacter to be interpreted as a literal (see note 3). When preceding a character without defined metacharacter meaning "\" and the character together match the character following the "\" (see note 4)
Metacharacter: [ ]; Indexing: Including the content; Description: Match any character within the specified set, see clause B.1.5.1 for more details

Metacharacter: -; Indexing: No effect, the surrounding set is indexed; Description: Has a metacharacter meaning in a set expression. It allows to specify a range of characters; see clause B.1.5.1 for more details

Metacharacter: ^; Indexing: No effect, the surrounding set is indexed; Description: Has a metacharacter meaning in a set expression. It causes to match any character complementing the set of characters following this metacharacter; see clause B.1.5.1 for more details

Metacharacter: \q{group,plane,row, cell} or \q{Uxxxx, Uxxx ….}; Indexing: Including the content enclosed within brackets; Description: Match one or more universal character. Both the quadruple and the USI-like syntaxes specified in clause 6.1.1 can be used
Metacharacter: {reference}; Indexing: Including the reference; Description: Insert the referenced user defined string and interpret it as a regular expression. See clause 27.9 for more details
Metacharacter: {\reference}; Indexing: Including the reference; Description: Insert the referenced user defined string and interpret it as a set of literals. See clause 27.9 for more details
Metacharacter: \N{reference}; Indexing: Including the reference; Description: Matches a single character from the (sub)set of characters denoted; see clause B.1.5.4 for more details
Metacharacter: \d; Description: Match any numerical digit (equivalent to [0-9])
Metacharacter: \w; Description: Match any alphanumeric character (equivalent to [0-9a-zA-Z])
Metacharacter: \t; Description: Match the control character CHARACTER TABULATION (0009) (see ISO/IEC 10646 [2])

Metacharacter: \n; Description: Match any of the following control characters: LINE FEED (000A), LINE TABULATION (000B), FORM FEED (000C), CARRIAGE RETURN (000D) (see ISO/IEC 10646 [2]) (jointly called newline characters
Metacharacter: \r; Description: Match the CARRIAGE RETURN (000D) control character (see ISO/IEC 10646 [2])

Metacharacter: \s; Description: Match any one of the following control characters defined in ISO/IEC 10646 [2]: CHARACTER TABULATION (0009), LINE FEED (000A), LINE TABULATION (000B), FORM FEED (000C), CARRIAGE RETURN (000D), all space characters defined in clause 17.2 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] and SP(32) defined in Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] (jointly called white-space characters)
Metacharacter: \b; Description: Match a word boundary (any graphical character except SP or DEL is preceded or followed by any of the whitespace or newline characters)
Metacharacter: \"; Description: Match the double quote character
Metacharacter: ""; Description: Match the double quote character
Metacharacter: Used to denote two alternative expressions
Metacharacter: ( ); Indexing: Including the content; Description: Used to group an expression

`#n` Including the Match the previous expression exactly n times (where n is a single digit) preceding (postfix); the same as #(n).

NOTE 1: Metacharacters ? and * are able to match any characters of the character set of the root type of the template or template field in which they are used (i.e. not considering type constraints applied).
However, it shall not be forgotten, that receiving operations require type checking of the received message before attempting to match it.
Therefore received values not complying with the subtype specification of the template or template field are never provided for matching.
NOTE 2: In some other languages/notations ? and * has different meaning as metacharacters.
However inTTCN-3 these characters are traditionally used for matching in the sense as specified in this table.

NOTE 3: Consequently the backslash character can be matched by a pair of backslash characters without space between them (\\), e.g. the pattern "\\d" will match the string "\d"; opening or closing square brackets can be matched by "\[" and "\]" respectively, etc.
NOTE 4: Such use of the metacharacter "\" is deprecated as further metacharacters can be defined later.
The symbols that can appear as lexical marks in metacharacter definitions are called metacharacter symbols.
When any of the metacharacter symbols are present in a pattern, but do not form a valid metacharacter, they retain their literal value.
NOTE: This rule assures that no format error can occur during pattern template instantiation.
However, errors caused by invalid references can still appear (see clauses 27.9 and B.1.5.4 for more details).
Character patterns may be composed from several fragments using the concatenation operation.
The fragments of the pattern shall be concatenated before any evaluation of the pattern expression.
See also the shorthand notation for referenced definitions at concatenation in clause 27.9.
EXAMPLE 3:

template charstring mw_myTemplate:= pattern "ab?\?" & "xyz*"; // results in the same pattern as
                                       // in example 2
Pattern definitions may contain references to values or templates.
The referred value or template shall be of the charstring or universal charstring type and it shall contain either a specific value or pattern.
When the referenced template contains a pattern, the character pattern definition of this pattern is used as a fragment for creating the new pattern.

A list of characters enclosed by a pair of "[" and "]" matches any single character in that list.
The set expression is delimited by the "[" "]" symbols.
In addition to character literals, it is possible to specify character ranges using the hyphen "-" as separator.
The range consist of the character immediately before the separator, the character immediately after it and all characters with a character code between the codes of the two bordering characters.
A hyphen character "-" inside the list but without preceding or following character loses its special meaning.
The set expression can also be negated by placing the caret "^" character as the first character after the opening square bracket.
Negation takes precedence over character ranges.
Therefore a hyphen "-" immediately following a negating caret "^" shall be processed as a literal character.

Metacharacter: #(n, m); Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression at least n times but no more than m times (postfix). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

Metacharacter: #n; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the previous expression exactly n times (where n is a single digit) (postfix); the same as #(n). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details
Metacharacter: +; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression one or several times (postfix); the same as #(1,). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

NOTE 1: Metacharacters ? and * are able to match any characters of the character set of the root type of the template or template field in which they are used (i.e. not considering type constraints applied).
However, it shall not be forgotten, that receiving operations require type checking of the received message before attempting to match it.
Therefore received values not complying with the subtype specification of the template or template field are never provided for matching.
NOTE 2: In some other languages/notations ? and * has different meaning as metacharacters.
However inTTCN-3 these characters are traditionally used for matching in the sense as specified in this table.

NOTE 3: Consequently the backslash character can be matched by a pair of backslash characters without space between them (\\), e.g. the pattern "\\d" will match the string "\d"; opening or closing square brackets can be matched by "\[" and "\]" respectively, etc. NOTE 4: Such use of the metacharacter "\" is deprecated as further metacharacters can be defined later.
Metacharacter; Indexing; Description
An empty list and an empty negated list are not allowed.

Therefore a closing square bracket "]" immediately following an opening square bracket "[" or a caret following the opening square bracket "[" and immediately followed by a closing square bracket "]" shall be processed as literal characters.
All metacharacters, except those listed below, lose their special meaning inside the list:
"]" not at the first position and not immediately following a "^" at the first position;
"-" not at the first or last positions in the list;
"^" at the first position in the list except when immediately followed by a closing square bracket;
"\q{group,plane,row,cell}";
"\N{reference}".
NOTE 1: Embedded lists are not allowed.

For example in pattern "[ab[r-z]]" the second "[" denotes a literal "[", the first "]" closes the list and the second "]" retains its literal value as no related opening bracket precedes it in the pattern.
The pattern will match character strings containing two elements, with the first element equal to "a", "b", "[" or anything in the range "r"-"z" and the second character equal to "]".
NOTE 2: To include a literal caret character "^", place it anywhere except in the first position or precede it with a backslash.
To include a literal hyphen "-", place it first or last in the list, or precede it with a backslash.
To include a literal closing square bracket "]", place it first or precede it with a backslash.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism

ambiguity.issue: 'type replicated by the set of' is used for the member type of the set of type.

improper_terms.used: type replicated by the set of
improper_terms.proper: member type of the set of type

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: The member type of the set of type associated with a SubSet and the member type of the template referenced in an `all from` clause of that SubSet SHALL be compatible.
requirements.original: c) The member type of the set of type associated with the SubSet and the member type of the template in the allfrom clause shall be compatible.

ambiguity.issue: The keyword is misspelled as 'allfrom'.

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL resolve either into a specific value or a combined template.
requirements.original: d) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a matching mechanism or combined template.

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'a matching mechanism or combined template', whereas the corresponding restrictions for template list, complement and SuperSet say 'a specific value or combined template', and EXAMPLE 2 of B.1.2.1/B.1.2.2 shows that an all from template resolving into a matching mechanism as a whole is an error. The 'specific value' reading is chosen as the likely intent.
readings: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL resolve either into a specific value or a combined template.
The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL resolve either into a matching mechanism or a combined template.

requirements.subject: ent:combined-template
requirements.canonical: An element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet MAY contain any matching mechanism or matching attribute except those prohibited by restriction e) of clause B.1.2.7.
requirements.original: Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SubSet's argument and an element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL NOT be `omit`, SuperSet, SubSet, a length restriction or `ifpresent`.
requirements.original: e) The individual members of the SubSet's argument and the elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not be the matching mechanisms omit, SuperSet, SubSet and the matching attributes (length restriction and ifpresent).

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SubSet's argument SHALL NOT resolve to AnyValueOrNone.
requirements.original: In addition, individual members shall not resolve to AnyValueOrNone

requirements.subject: ent:combined-template
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL NOT resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
requirements.original: individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.condition: a length matching attribute is attached to the SubSet
requirements.canonical: If a length matching attribute is attached to a SubSet, the maximum length allowed by the length attribute SHALL NOT exceed the number of elements in the SubSet.
requirements.original: f) If the length matching attribute is attached to the SubSet, the maximum length allowed by the length attribute shall not exceed the number of the elements in the SubSet.

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: A template in a SubSet's argument SHALL obey the present template restriction.
requirements.original: g) Templates in SubSet's argument shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: The keyword `omit` IS the notation denoting that an optional field of a record or set, or a specific key within a map, is absent.
requirements.original: The keyword omit denotes that an optional field of a record or set or a specific key within a map shall be absent.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: When used as a matching mechanism, `omit` matches an optional field or a map key if, and only if, the field or key is absent.
requirements.original: If used as a matching mechanism, it matches an optional field or a map key if and only if it is absent.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: `omit` MAY be assigned to a template of any type as a whole, to an optional field of a set or record template, or to a value associated with a key of a map template.
requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: `omit` SHALL NOT be assigned to a mandatory field of a record or set template.
requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.condition: matching during a receiving operation
requirements.canonical: At the time of matching during a receiving operation, `omit` SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.
requirements.original: b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether a template that is `omit` as a whole (allowed by restriction a) may be used directly in a receiving operation, and whether a violation is a compile-time or a runtime error. The reading that a top-level `omit` is not allowed in a receiving operation is chosen.
readings: A template that is `omit` as a whole SHALL NOT be used as the top-level template of a receiving operation.
A template that is `omit` as a whole MAY be used in a receiving operation only when referenced from an optional field or map value; otherwise the matching causes a runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol (`decmatch`) IS used for checking encoded payload fields.
requirements.original: The matching symbol MatchDecodedContent `decmatch is used for checking encoded payload fields.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol IS composed of the `decmatch` keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance.
requirements.original: The matching` symbol is composed of the decmatch keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance called decoding target.

requirements.subject: ent:decoding-target
requirements.canonical: The mandatory template instance of a MatchDecodedContent matching symbol IS called decoding target.
requirements.original: The matching` symbol is composed of the decmatch keyword, an optional encoding format parameter and a mandatory template instance called decoding target.

requirements.subject: ent:template-field
requirements.condition: the template field uses the MatchDecodedContent matching symbol
requirements.canonical: A template field that uses `decmatch` matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field can be successfully decoded as an instance of the same type as the decoding target and the decoded instance is successfully matched by the decoding target.
requirements.original: A template field that uses this symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field can be successfully decoded as an instance of the same type as the decoding target and if the decoded instance can be successfully matched by the decoding target.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` MAY specify one of the UCS encoding formats.
requirements.original: The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter is present
requirements.canonical: If the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` is present, the specified encoding format SHALL be used for the decoding trial.
requirements.original: The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter is present
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or to the type of the decoding target.
requirements.original: The optional encoding format parameter may specify one of the UCS encoding formats (see clause C.5.4) that shall be used for the decoding trial, i.e. it overrides any variant attribute attached to the decoding target or the type of the decoding target (for example, for predefined variant attributes see clause 27.5).

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol SHALL be assigned only to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.
requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be assigned' in a Restrictions list; chose the restrictive reading (only these types).
readings: The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol SHALL be assigned only to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types.

The MatchDecodedContent matching symbol MAY be assigned to templates and template fields of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring and universal charstring types (other types not explicitly excluded).

requirements.subject: ent:decoding-target
requirements.canonical: The decoding target of `decmatch` MAY be a template of any data type.
requirements.original: b) The decoding target can be a template of any data type.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be used only for template fields of universal charstring type.
requirements.original: c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).

ambiguity.issue: The source text is garbled ('fields of r universal charstring types'), and restriction d) implies an encoding format also applies to charstring fields; chose universal charstring only, as literally written.
readings: The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be used only for template fields of universal charstring type.
The encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be used only for template fields of charstring or universal charstring type.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be of charstring type.
requirements.original: c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` SHALL be one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` predefined function.
requirements.original: c) The optional encoding format parameter can be used only for fields of r universal `charstring types.` The parameter value shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar predefined function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter value is not one of the strings allowed for decvalue_unichar
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of `decmatch` that is not one of the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated whether the error is a compile-time or a runtime error; chose 'an error' generically (compile-time if the value is known statically, otherwise runtime).
readings: An encoding format parameter value of `decmatch` that is not allowed SHALL cause a compile-time error.
An encoding format parameter value of `decmatch` that is not allowed SHALL cause a runtime error when matching is performed.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the template field is of charstring or universal charstring type and the encoding format parameter is missing
requirements.canonical: If the template field is of charstring or universal charstring type and the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` is missing, the encoding format "UTF-8" SHALL be used.
requirements.original: d) If the template field is of charstring type or is of universal charstring type and the encoding format is missing, the default value "UTF-8" shall be used.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: Before `decmatch` decoding, hexstring and octetstring values are implicitly converted to bitstring values using the predefined functions `hex2bit` and `oct2bit`.
requirements.original: At first, hexstring and octetstring values are implicitly converted to a bitstring value using the predefined hex2bit and oct2bit functions (specified in clauses C.1.18 and C.1.22) and charstring values are implicitly converted to universal charstring values.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: Before `decmatch` decoding, charstring values are implicitly converted to universal charstring values.
requirements.original: At first, hexstring and octetstring values are implicitly converted to a bitstring value using the predefined hex2bit and oct2bit functions (specified in clauses C.1.18 and C.1.22) and charstring values are implicitly converted to universal charstring values.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: Prior to `decmatch` decoding, the bitstring or universal charstring value is stored into a temporary anonymous variable.
requirements.original: Prior to decoding, the bitstring and universal charstring values are stored into a temporary anonymous variable.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: `decmatch` decoding of bitstring values is performed by implicitly calling the predefined function `decvalue`.
requirements.original: Decoding is then performed by implicitly calling the predefined decvalue function (specified in clause C.5.2) for bitstring values and decvalue_unichar function for universal charstring values.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: `decmatch` decoding of universal charstring values is performed by implicitly calling the predefined function `decvalue_unichar`.
requirements.original: Decoding is then performed by implicitly calling the predefined decvalue function (specified in clause C.5.2) for bitstring values and decvalue_unichar function for universal charstring values.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: In `decmatch` decoding, the anonymous variable containing the encoded value is passed as the first parameter to the decoding function.
requirements.original: The anonymous variable containing the encoded value is passed as the first parameter to the function, the second parameter contains another temporary variable called decoded instance.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-instance
requirements.canonical: In `decmatch` decoding, the second parameter of the decoding function is a temporary variable called decoded instance.
requirements.original: The anonymous variable containing the encoded value is passed as the first parameter to the function, the second parameter contains another temporary variable called decoded instance.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-instance
requirements.canonical: The decoded instance IS of the same type as the decoding target.
requirements.original: The decoded instance is of the same type as the decoding target.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the encoding format parameter is present
requirements.canonical: If the encoding format parameter of `decmatch` is present, it is passed as the third parameter to the `decvalue_unichar` function.
requirements.original: If the optional encoding format parameter is present, it is passed as the third parameter to the decvalue_unichar function.

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: `decmatch` decoding IS successful only if the decoding function returns 0 and the first parameter contains an empty string after decoding.
requirements.original: Decoding is successful only if the decoding function returns 0 and the first parameter contains an empty string (i.e. the whole encoded value has been successfully decoded).

requirements.subject: ent:match-decoded-content
requirements.canonical: The MatchDecodedContent matching mechanism produces an unsuccessful match if decoding has not succeeded.
requirements.original: The matching mechanism will generate an unsuccessful match if decoding hasn't succeeded.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.condition: the enumerated value has an associated value list in its definition
requirements.canonical: To match an enumerated value with an associated value list, the template SHALL reference the enumerated value name followed by a list of integer templates in parentheses.
requirements.original: To match an enumerated value with an associated value list in its definition, the enumerated value name shall be referenced followed by a non-empty list of integer templates in parenthesis.

requirements.subject: ent:integer-template
requirements.canonical: The list of integer templates following an enumerated value name in a template SHALL NOT be empty.
requirements.original: To match an enumerated value with an associated value list in its definition, the enumerated value name shall be referenced followed by a non-empty list of integer templates in parenthesis.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template of the form enumerated value name followed by a list of integer templates matches only enumerated values of the same name whose associated integer value is matched by at least one of the integer templates.
requirements.original: The template matches only those enumerated values of the same name where the associated integer values is matched by at least one of the integer templates.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: The matching mechanisms of clause B.1.3 MAY be used inside explicit values of strings, record of types, set of types, arrays or maps.
requirements.original: The following matching mechanisms may be used inside explicit values of strings, records of, sets of, arrays or maps.

requirements.subject: ent:combined-template
requirements.canonical: A template that contains a matching mechanism inside a value IS called a combined template.
requirements.original: The template that contains a matching mechanism inside a value is called a combined template.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: The matching symbol "?" (AnyElement) replaces a single element of a string (except character strings), a record of, a set of or an array.
requirements.original: The matching symbol "?" (AnyElement) is used to indicate that it replaces single elements of a string (except character strings, see table 4 for the lengths of the units being matched by "?" in a string), a record of, a set of or an array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: The length of the unit matched by AnyElement in a string IS given by table 4.
requirements.original: The matching symbol "?" (AnyElement) is used to indicate that it replaces single elements of a string (except character strings, see table 4 for the lengths of the units being matched by "?" in a string), a record of, a set of or an array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: AnyElement SHALL be used only within values of string types, record of types, set of types and arrays.
requirements.original: a) It shall be used only within values of string types, record of types, set of types and arrays.

ambiguity.issue: 'string types' includes character string types, although B.1.3.1.0 and B.1.3.1.1 state that "?" inside character strings is a literal character and that character patterns shall be used instead; chose the reading that excludes character strings.
readings: AnyElement SHALL be used only within values of binary string types (bitstring, hexstring, octetstring), record of types, set of types and arrays.
AnyElement SHALL be used only within values of any string type (including character strings), record of types, set of types and arrays.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: A "?" inside a record of, set of or array value of an integer element type can be interpreted either as AnyValue for the integer element or as AnyElement.
requirements.original: NOTE: The "?" in field4 can be interpreted as AnyValue as an integer value, or AnyElement inside a record of, set of or array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: Interpreting "?" inside a record of, set of or array value as AnyValue or as AnyElement leads to the same matching result.
requirements.original: Since both interpretations lead to the same match no problem arises.

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A "?" wildcard in character strings SHALL be expressed using a character pattern.
requirements.original: If it is required to express the "?" wildcard in character strings it shall be done using character patterns (see clause B.1.5).

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: The character pattern `pattern "abc?xyz"` IS matched by character strings such as "abcdxyz", "abccxyz" and "abcxxyz".
requirements.original: For example: "abcdxyz", "abccxyz", "abcxxyz" etc. will all match pattern "abc?xyz".

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: The character pattern `pattern "abc?xyz"` IS NOT matched by character strings such as "abcxyz" and "abcdefxyz".
requirements.original: However, "abcxyz", "abcdefxyz", etc. will not.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: The matching symbol "*" (AnyElementsOrNone) replaces none or any number of consecutive elements of a string (except character strings), a record of, a set of or an array.
requirements.original: The matching symbol "*" (AnyElementsOrNone) is used to indicate that it replaces none or any number of consecutive elements of a string (except character strings), a record of, a set of or an array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyElementsOrNone matches the longest sequence of elements possible according to the pattern specified by the symbols surrounding the "*".
requirements.original: The "*" symbol matches the longest sequence of elements possible, according to the pattern as specified by the symbols surrounding the "*".

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyElementsOrNone in a map template replaces none or any number of elements whose keys are not present in the map template.
requirements.original: _AnyElementsOrNone is also used in templates of a map type where it replaces none or any number of elements whose_ keys are not present in the map template.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: A "*" appearing at the highest level inside a binary string, record of, set of or array value SHALL be interpreted as AnyElementsOrNone.
requirements.original: If a "*" appears at the highest level inside a binary string, a record of, set of or array, it shall be interpreted as _AnyElementsOrNone._

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: A "*" at the highest level inside a binary string, record of, set of or array value IS NOT interpreted as AnyValueOrNone replacing a single element.
requirements.original: NOTE: This rule prevents the otherwise possible interpretation of "*" as AnyValueOrNone that replaces an element inside a binary string, record of, set of or array.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be used only within values of binary string types, record of types, set of types, map types and arrays, and inside the permutation matching mechanism.
requirements.original: a) It shall be used only within values of binary string types, record of types, set of, map types and arrays and inside the permutation matching mechanism.

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A "*" wildcard in character strings SHALL be expressed using a character pattern.
requirements.original: If it is required to expressed the "*" wildcard in character strings it shall be done using character patterns (see clause B.1.5).

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: The character pattern `pattern "abc*xyz"` IS matched by character strings such as "abcxyz", "abcdefxyz" and "abcabcxyz".
requirements.original: For example: "abcxyz", "abcdefxyz" "abcabcxyz" etc. will all match pattern "abc*xyz".

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: Permutation SHALL be used only on values of record of and array types.
requirements.original: _Permutation is an operation for matching that shall be used only on values of record of and array types._ _Permutation is denoted by the keyword permutation.

ambiguity.issue: Permutation is called 'an operation for matching'; elsewhere it is a matching mechanism (used inside values).

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: Permutation IS denoted by the keyword `permutation`.
requirements.original: _Permutation is an operation for matching that shall be used only on values of record of and array types._ _Permutation is denoted by the keyword permutation.

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.condition: the permutation contains no AnyElementsOrNone
requirements.canonical: A permutation without AnyElementsOrNone in place of a single record of element matches any series of elements for which there is a one-to-one mapping between the elements in the record of value and in the permutation list such that each element matches its corresponding element in the permutation list.
requirements.original: A permutation without AnyElementsOrNone in place of a single record of element means that any series of elements is acceptable provided that there is a one to one mapping between elements in the record of and in the permutation list such that each element matches its corresponding element in the permutation list.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.condition: AnyElementsOrNone is used inside a permutation
requirements.canonical: AnyElementsOrNone used inside a permutation, directly or via reference, replaces none or any number of elements within the segment of the record of value matched by the permutation.
requirements.original: _AnyElementsOrNone used inside permutation (directly or via reference) replaces none or any number of elements_ within the segment of the record of value matched by permutation.

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.condition: the permutation contains AnyElementsOrNone
requirements.canonical: A permutation containing AnyElementsOrNone matches successfully if a subset of the elements in the record of value matches the permutation list without the AnyElementsOrNone.
requirements.original: The permutation matching is successful, if a subset of the elements in the record of matches the permutation list without the AnyElementsOrNone.

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.condition: both permutation and AnyElementsOrNone are used in a record of template
requirements.canonical: If both permutation and AnyElementsOrNone are used in a record of template, they SHALL be evaluated jointly.
requirements.original: If both permutation and _AnyElementsOrNone are used in a record of template, they shall be evaluated jointly._

ambiguity.issue: 'evaluated jointly' is not defined; chose the reading that the whole template is matched as one pattern (all possible element assignments considered), not permutation first and AnyElementsOrNone afterwards.
readings: If both permutation and AnyElementsOrNone are used in a record of template, the matcher SHALL consider all assignments of elements to the permutation and to AnyElementsOrNone together (one combined pattern).
If both permutation and AnyElementsOrNone are used in a record of template, the matcher SHALL match the permutation and the AnyElementsOrNone in a single left-to-right pass without backtracking.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyElementsOrNone used in conjunction with a permutation (outside it) replaces consecutive elements only, unlike AnyElementsOrNone used inside a permutation.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _AnyElementsOrNone used inside permutation has a different effect as AnyElementsOrNone used in_ conjunction with permutation as in the latter AnyElementsOrNone replaces consecutive elements only.

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: The template {permutation(1,2,*)} IS equivalent to ({*,1,*,2,*},{*,2,*,1,*}), while {permutation(1,2),*} IS equivalent to ({1,2,*},{2,1,*}).
requirements.original: For example, {permutation(1,2,*)} is equivalent to ({*,1,*,2,*},{*,2,*,1,*}), while {permutation(1,2),*} is equivalent to ({1,2,*},{2,1,*}).

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: A length attribute MAY be applied to AnyElementsOrNone inside a permutation to restrict the number of elements matched by AnyElementsOrNone.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: When AnyElementsOrNone is inside a permutation, a length attribute may be applied to _AnyElementsOrNone to restrict the number of elements matched by AnyElementsOrNone (see also_ clause B.1.4.1).

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: All elements of a record of or set of template MAY be added into a permutation using an `all from` clause.
requirements.original: Besides specifying all individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into permutations using an all from clause.

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: Each individual member listed in a permutation SHALL be of the type replicated by the record of or array type.
requirements.original: a) Each individual member listed in the permutation shall be of the type replicated by the record of or array type.

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: The member type of the permutation and the member type of the template in the `all from` clause SHALL be compatible.
requirements.original: b) The member type of the permutation and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: The template referenced in an `all from` clause inside a permutation SHALL resolve into either a specific value or a combined template.
requirements.original: c) The template referenced in the all from clause shall resolve either into specific value (see clause B.1.1) or combined template.

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: A combined template referenced in an `all from` clause inside a permutation SHALL NOT contain permutations.
requirements.original: The combined template shall not contain permutations.

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: Each template other than AnyElementsOrNone listed in a permutation SHALL obey the present template restriction.
requirements.original: e) Templates except AnyElementsOrNone listed in the permutation shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.subject: ent:matching-attribute
requirements.canonical: The matching attributes of clause B.1.4 (length restriction and ifpresent) MAY be associated with matching mechanisms.
requirements.original: The following attributes may be associated with matching mechanisms.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The length restriction attribute restricts the length of string values matching the template or the number of elements in a set of, record of or array value.
requirements.original: The length restriction attribute is used to restrict the length of string values matching the template or the number of elements in a set `of, record` `of or array structure.`

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The length restriction attribute MAY be used in conjunction with the ifpresent matching attribute.
requirements.original: It can also be used in conjunction with the ifpresent matching attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: When the length attribute is used with a template list, elements of the template list whose lengths do not satisfy the length attribute can never match (are disabled).
requirements.original: NOTE: When the length attribute is used with a template list, elements of the list may be disabled by the attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: For string values, the unit of length of a length restriction IS interpreted according to table 4.
requirements.original: The units of length are to be interpreted according to table 4 in the main body of the present document in the case of string values.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction

requirements.canonical: The length restriction SHALL NOT be used directly with templates and template fields produced by concatenation.

requirements.original: c) The boundaries of the length restriction shall be denoted by expressions which resolve to specific non-negative integer values.
