ambiguity.issue: Table B.1 does not define what the "Indexing" column means; it most likely describes how far the metacharacter extends when positions/groups of a pattern are counted (e.g. for the regexp function). That reading was chosen.
readings: For indexing, the metacharacter `( )` includes its content.
The "Indexing" entry describes which characters of the pattern are counted as one item when the preceding-expression postfix metacharacters (#(n,m), #n, +) are applied.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-any-char
requirements.canonical: The metacharacters `?` and `*` CAN match any character of the character set of the root type of the template or template field in which they are used, without considering applied type constraints.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Metacharacters ? and * are able to match any characters of the character set of the root type of the template or template field in which they are used (i.e. not considering type constraints applied).

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: A receiving operation SHALL type-check a received message before attempting to match it.
requirements.original: However, it shall not be forgotten, that receiving operations require type checking of the received message before attempting to match it.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: A received value not complying with the subtype specification of the template or template field IS NOT provided for matching.
requirements.original: Therefore received values not complying with the subtype specification of the template or template field are never provided for matching.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-any-char
requirements.canonical: In some other languages or notations the characters `?` and `*` have a different meaning as metacharacters.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: In some other languages/notations ? and * has different meaning as metacharacters.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-any-char
requirements.canonical: In TTCN-3 the characters `?` and `*` are used for matching in the sense specified in table B.1.
requirements.original: However inTTCN-3 these characters are traditionally used for matching in the sense as specified in this table.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-backslash
requirements.canonical: A backslash character CAN be matched by a pair of backslash characters "\\" without space between them, and opening or closing square brackets CAN be matched by "\[" and "\]".
requirements.original: NOTE 3: Consequently the backslash character can be matched by a pair of backslash characters without space between them (\\), e.g. the pattern "\\d" will match the string "\d"; opening or closing square brackets can be matched by "\[" and "\]" respectively, etc.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-backslash
requirements.condition: "\" precedes a character without defined metacharacter meaning
requirements.canonical: Using "\" before a character without defined metacharacter meaning IS deprecated, as further metacharacters can be defined later.
requirements.original: NOTE 4: Such use of the metacharacter "\" is deprecated as further metacharacters can be defined later.

requirements.subject: ent:metacharacter-symbol
requirements.canonical: A metacharacter symbol IS a symbol that can appear as a lexical mark in a metacharacter definition.
requirements.original: The symbols that can appear as lexical marks in metacharacter definitions are called metacharacter symbols.

requirements.subject: ent:metacharacter-symbol
requirements.canonical: The metacharacter symbols ARE the characters "#", "(", ")", "*", "+", "-", "?", "[", "\", "]", "^", "{", "|" and "}".

requirements.subject: ent:metacharacter-symbol
requirements.condition: the metacharacter symbol does not form a valid metacharacter
requirements.canonical: A metacharacter symbol present in a pattern that does not form a valid metacharacter retains its literal value.
requirements.original: When any of the metacharacter symbols are present in a pattern, but do not form a valid metacharacter, they retain their literal value.

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A format error CANNOT occur during pattern template instantiation.
requirements.original: NOTE: This rule assures that no format error can occur during pattern template instantiation.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: An error caused by an invalid reference CAN still occur during pattern template instantiation.
requirements.original: However, errors caused by invalid references can still appear (see clauses 27.9 and B.1.5.4 for more details).

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A character pattern MAY be composed from several fragments using the concatenation operation.
requirements.original: Character patterns may be composed from several fragments using the concatenation operation.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern-fragment
requirements.canonical: The fragments of a character pattern SHALL be concatenated before any evaluation of the pattern expression.
requirements.original: The fragments of the pattern shall be concatenated before any evaluation of the pattern expression.

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A pattern definition MAY contain references to values or templates.
requirements.original: Pattern definitions may contain references to values or templates.

requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.canonical: A value or template referenced in a pattern definition SHALL be of the `charstring` or `universal charstring` type.
requirements.original: The referred value or template shall be of the charstring or universal charstring type and it shall contain either a specific value or pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A value or template referenced in a pattern definition SHALL contain either a specific value or a pattern.
requirements.original: The referred value or template shall be of the charstring or universal charstring type and it shall contain either a specific value or pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.condition: the referenced template contains a pattern
requirements.canonical: When a referenced template contains a pattern, the character pattern definition of that pattern IS used as a fragment for creating the new pattern.
requirements.original: When the referenced template contains a pattern, the character pattern definition of this pattern is used as a fragment for creating the new pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A list of characters enclosed by "[" and "]" matches any single character in that list.
requirements.original: A list of characters enclosed by a pair of "[" and "]" matches any single character in that list.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A set expression IS delimited by the "[" and "]" symbols.
requirements.original: The set expression is delimited by the "[" "]" symbols.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A set expression MAY specify character ranges using the hyphen "-" as separator, in addition to character literals.
requirements.original: In addition to character literals, it is possible to specify character ranges using the hyphen "-" as separator.

requirements.subject: ent:character-range
requirements.canonical: A character range consists of the character immediately before the separator, the character immediately after it, and all characters with a character code between the codes of these two bordering characters.
requirements.original: The range consist of the character immediately before the separator, the character immediately after it and all characters with a character code between the codes of the two bordering characters.

ambiguity.issue: "consist" should be "consists"; "range" means character range in a set expression.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hyphen
requirements.canonical: A hyphen "-" inside a set expression without a preceding or following character loses its special meaning.
requirements.original: A hyphen character "-" inside the list but without preceding or following character loses its special meaning.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A set expression MAY be negated by placing the caret "^" as the first character after the opening square bracket.
requirements.original: The set expression can also be negated by placing the caret "^" character as the first character after the opening square bracket.

requirements.subject: ent:negated-set-expression
requirements.canonical: Negation takes precedence over character ranges in a set expression.
requirements.original: Negation takes precedence over character ranges.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hyphen
requirements.canonical: A hyphen "-" immediately following a negating caret "^" SHALL be processed as a literal character.
requirements.original: Therefore a hyphen "-" immediately following a negating caret "^" shall be processed as a literal character.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-repetition
requirements.canonical: The postfix metacharacter `#(n, m)` matches the preceding expression at least n times but no more than m times.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: #(n, m); Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression at least n times but no more than m times (postfix). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-repetition
requirements.canonical: For indexing, the metacharacter `#(n, m)` includes the preceding expression.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: #(n, m); Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression at least n times but no more than m times (postfix). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

ambiguity.issue: Table B.1 does not define what the "Indexing" column means; it most likely describes how far the metacharacter extends when positions/groups of a pattern are counted (e.g. for the regexp function). That reading was chosen.
readings: For indexing, the metacharacter `#(n, m)` includes the preceding expression.
The "Indexing" entry describes which characters of the pattern are counted as one item when the preceding-expression postfix metacharacters (#(n,m), #n, +) are applied.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hash-n
requirements.canonical: The postfix metacharacter `#n`, where n is a single digit, matches the preceding expression exactly n times and is equivalent to `#(n)`.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: #n; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the previous expression exactly n times (where n is a single digit) (postfix); the same as #(n). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

ambiguity.issue: The row says "previous expression" while the other rows say "preceding expression".

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hash-n
requirements.canonical: For indexing, the metacharacter `#n` includes the preceding expression.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: #n; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the previous expression exactly n times (where n is a single digit) (postfix); the same as #(n). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

ambiguity.issue: Table B.1 does not define what the "Indexing" column means; it most likely describes how far the metacharacter extends when positions/groups of a pattern are counted (e.g. for the regexp function). That reading was chosen.
readings: For indexing, the metacharacter `#n` includes the preceding expression.
The "Indexing" entry describes which characters of the pattern are counted as one item when the preceding-expression postfix metacharacters (#(n,m), #n, +) are applied.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-plus
requirements.canonical: The postfix metacharacter `+` matches the preceding expression one or more times and is equivalent to `#(1,)`.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: +; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression one or several times (postfix); the same as #(1,). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-plus
requirements.canonical: For indexing, the metacharacter `+` includes the preceding expression.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: +; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression one or several times (postfix); the same as #(1,). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

ambiguity.issue: Table B.1 does not define what the "Indexing" column means; it most likely describes how far the metacharacter extends when positions/groups of a pattern are counted (e.g. for the regexp function). That reading was chosen.
readings: For indexing, the metacharacter `+` includes the preceding expression.
The "Indexing" entry describes which characters of the pattern are counted as one item when the preceding-expression postfix metacharacters (#(n,m), #n, +) are applied.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A set expression SHALL NOT be an empty list.
requirements.original: An empty list and an empty negated list are not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:negated-set-expression
requirements.canonical: A negated set expression SHALL NOT be an empty negated list.
requirements.original: An empty list and an empty negated list are not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A closing square bracket "]" immediately following an opening square bracket "[" SHALL be processed as a literal character.
requirements.original: Therefore a closing square bracket "]" immediately following an opening square bracket "[" or a caret following the opening square bracket "[" and immediately followed by a closing square bracket "]" shall be processed as literal characters.

requirements.subject: ent:negated-set-expression
requirements.canonical: A caret "^" following the opening square bracket "[" and immediately followed by a closing square bracket "]" SHALL be processed as a literal character, together with that "]".
requirements.original: Therefore a closing square bracket "]" immediately following an opening square bracket "[" or a caret following the opening square bracket "[" and immediately followed by a closing square bracket "]" shall be processed as literal characters.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether both "^" and the following "]" become literals (the list then continues) or only the "]". Chosen reading: both are literal, consistent with list item B.1.5.1-s024.
readings: In "[^]", both the caret and the closing bracket SHALL be processed as literal characters.
In "[^]", only the closing bracket SHALL be processed as a literal character and the caret keeps its negating meaning.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, every metacharacter except those listed in clause B.1.5.1 loses its special meaning.
requirements.original: All metacharacters, except those listed below, lose their special meaning inside the list:

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, "]" keeps its metacharacter meaning when it is not at the first position and does not immediately follow a "^" at the first position.
requirements.original: "]" not at the first position and not immediately following a "^" at the first position;

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hyphen
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, "-" keeps its metacharacter meaning when it is not at the first or last position in the list.
requirements.original: "-" not at the first or last positions in the list;

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-caret
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, "^" keeps its metacharacter meaning when it is at the first position in the list and is not immediately followed by a closing square bracket.
requirements.original: "^" at the first position in the list except when immediately followed by a closing square bracket;

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, the metacharacters "\", "\d", "\t", "\w", "\r", "\n", "\s" and "\b" keep their metacharacter meaning.

ambiguity.issue: Meaning of the word-boundary metacharacter "\b" inside a set expression (which matches one character) is not defined.
readings: Inside a set expression, "\b" keeps its word-boundary meaning.
Inside a set expression, "\b" denotes some single character (e.g. backspace) rather than a word boundary.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-q
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, the metacharacter "\q{group,plane,row,cell}" keeps its metacharacter meaning.
requirements.original: "\q{group,plane,row,cell}";

ambiguity.issue: Only the quadruple form is listed; unclear whether the USI-like form \q{Uxxxx} also keeps its meaning inside a set expression.
readings: Inside a set expression, only the quadruple form of "\q" keeps its metacharacter meaning.
Inside a set expression, both the quadruple and the USI-like forms of "\q" keep their metacharacter meaning.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-n-reference
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, the metacharacter "\N{reference}" keeps its metacharacter meaning.
requirements.original: "\N{reference}".

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: An embedded set expression IS NOT allowed inside a set expression.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Embedded lists are not allowed.

ambiguity.issue: "lists" means set expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: In the pattern "[ab[r-z]]" the second "[" denotes a literal "[", the first "]" closes the set expression and the second "]" retains its literal value.
requirements.original: For example in pattern "[ab[r-z]]" the second "[" denotes a literal "[", the first "]" closes the list and the second "]" retains its literal value as no related opening bracket precedes it in the pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: The pattern "[ab[r-z]]" matches a two-character string whose first character is "a", "b", "[" or in the range "r"-"z" and whose second character is "]".
requirements.original: The pattern will match character strings containing two elements, with the first element equal to "a", "b", "[" or anything in the range "r"-"z" and the second character equal to "]".

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-caret
requirements.canonical: A literal caret "^" CAN be included in a set expression by placing it anywhere except the first position or by preceding it with a backslash.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: To include a literal caret character "^", place it anywhere except in the first position or precede it with a backslash.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hyphen
requirements.canonical: A literal hyphen "-" CAN be included in a set expression by placing it first or last in the list or by preceding it with a backslash.
requirements.original: To include a literal hyphen "-", place it first or last in the list, or precede it with a backslash.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A literal closing square bracket "]" CAN be included in a set expression by placing it first or by preceding it with a backslash.
requirements.original: To include a literal closing square bracket "]", place it first or precede it with a backslash.

requirements.subject: ent:negated-set-expression
requirements.condition: the first character in the set expression is "^"
requirements.canonical: If the first character in a set expression is the caret "^", the characters "-" and "]" match themselves when they immediately follow that caret.
requirements.original: If the first character in the list is the caret "^", then the characters "-" and "]" also match themselves when they immediately follow that caret.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: A character pattern MAY contain references to templates, constants, variables, formal parameters, module parameters, or fields of these, containing either a character string value or a pattern.
requirements.original: In addition to direct string values, it is also possible within the pattern to use references to templates, constants, variables, formal parameters, module parameters, or to their fields, containing either a character string value or pattern matching.

ambiguity.issue: "pattern matching" is used where a pattern (matching mechanism) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: A reference in a pattern SHALL be enclosed within the "{" and "}" characters.
requirements.original: The reference shall be enclosed within the "{" "}" characters and reference shall resolve a compatible character string type.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: A reference in a pattern SHALL resolve to a compatible character string type.
requirements.original: The reference shall be enclosed within the "{" "}" characters and reference shall resolve a compatible character string type.

ambiguity.issue: "compatible character string type" does not say compatible with what; chosen: compatible with the type of the pattern being constructed.
readings: A reference in a pattern SHALL resolve to an entity whose type is compatible with the character string type of the pattern being constructed.
A reference in a pattern SHALL resolve to an entity of any character string type (charstring or universal charstring).

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: The opening bracket "{" of a reference expression MAY be followed by a backslash.
requirements.original: The opening bracket can be optionally followed by a backslash.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-reference
requirements.condition: the opening bracket is not followed by a backslash
requirements.canonical: If the backslash is missing, the referenced character string or pattern SHALL be inserted into the pattern being constructed and SHALL be handled as a regular expression.
requirements.original: If the backslash character is missing, the referenced character string or pattern shall be inserted into the pattern being constructed and shall be handled as a regular expression.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: Each reference expression SHALL be dereferenced only once, before insertion; the dereferenced and inserted content SHALL NOT be dereferenced again.
requirements.original: Each expression shall be dereferenced only once, before the insertion (i.e. the expression dereferenced and inserted into the referencing pattern shall not be dereferenced again).

ambiguity.issue: "expression" means reference expression.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-literal-reference
requirements.condition: the opening bracket is followed by a backslash
requirements.canonical: If the backslash is present, the referenced item SHALL contain a character string value.
requirements.original: If the backslash character is present, the referenced item shall contain a character string value in this case.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-literal-reference
requirements.condition: the opening bracket is followed by a backslash
requirements.canonical: If the backslash is present, the referenced character string IS inserted into the pattern so that all its characters keep their literal value, i.e. all metacharacter symbols are automatically escaped.
requirements.original: The character string is inserted into the pattern being constructed so that it all characters contained in it can keep their literal value (i.e. all metacharacter symbols are automatically escaped).

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the reference cannot be resolved or the referenced symbol does not fulfil the requirements
requirements.canonical: If a reference in a pattern cannot be resolved, or the referenced symbol does not fulfil the requirements of clause B.1.5.2, an error SHALL be generated.
requirements.original: If the reference cannot be resolved or if the referenced symbol does not fulfil the requirements set by this clause, an error shall be generated.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.condition: the referenced definition or field contains reference expressions
requirements.canonical: If a referenced definition or field contains one or more reference expressions, those references SHALL be recursively dereferenced before its contents are inserted into the referencing pattern.
requirements.original: If a referenced definition or field of a definition contains one or more reference expressions, then these references shall recursively be dereferenced before inserting their contents into the referencing pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern-fragment
requirements.condition: the pattern fragment contains a single reference only
requirements.canonical: If a pattern fragment contains a single reference only, the definition or field MAY be referenced directly, omitting the double quotes and the curly brackets.
requirements.original: If a fragment of a pattern contains a single reference only, it is allowed, as a shorthand notation, to reference the definition or the field of the definition directly, i.e. leave out double quotes (" ") and the pair of curly brackets ({ }).

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: A pattern expression that is to be matched a number of times SHALL be followed by one of the postfixes "#(n, m)", "#(n, )", "#(, m)", "#(n)", "#n", "#(,)", "#()" or "+".
requirements.original: To specify that the preceding expression should be matched a number of times one of the following syntaxes shall be used: "#(n, m)", "#(n, )", "#(, m)", "#(n)", "#n", "#(,)", "#()" or "+".

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "#(n, m)" SHALL match the preceding expression at least n times and not more than m times.
requirements.original: The form "#(n, m)" specifies that the preceding expression shall be matched at least n times but not more than m times.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "#(n, )" SHALL match the preceding expression at least n times.
requirements.original: The metacharacter postfix "#(n, )" specifies that the preceding expression shall be matched at least n times while "#(, m)" indicates that the preceding expression shall be matched not more than m times.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "#(, m)" SHALL match the preceding expression not more than m times.
requirements.original: The metacharacter postfix "#(n, )" specifies that the preceding expression shall be matched at least n times while "#(, m)" indicates that the preceding expression shall be matched not more than m times.

ambiguity.issue: The lower bound of "#(, m)" is not stated; by analogy with "#(,)" being "#(0,)", 0 is assumed.
readings: The postfix "#(, m)" SHALL match the preceding expression 0 to m times.
The postfix "#(, m)" SHALL match the preceding expression 1 to m times.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfixes "#(n)" and "#n" SHALL match the preceding expression exactly n times.
requirements.original: Metacharacters (postfixes) "#(n)" and "#n" specify that the preceding expression shall be matched exactly n times (they are equivalent to "#(n, n)").

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfixes "#(n)" and "#n" ARE equivalent to "#(n, n)".
requirements.original: Metacharacters (postfixes) "#(n)" and "#n" specify that the preceding expression shall be matched exactly n times (they are equivalent to "#(n, n)").

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: In the postfix form "#n", n SHALL be a single digit.
requirements.original: In the form "#n" n shall be a single digit.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfixes "#(,)" and "#()" ARE shorthand notations for "#(0,)" and match the preceding expression any number of times.
requirements.original: The forms "#(,)" and "#()" are shorthand notations for "#(0,)", i.e. matches the preceding expression any number of times.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "+" SHALL match the preceding expression at least 1 time.
requirements.original: The metacharacter postfix "+" denotes that the preceding expression shall be matched at least 1 time (equivalent to "#(1,)").

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "+" IS equivalent to "#(1,)".
requirements.original: The metacharacter postfix "+" denotes that the preceding expression shall be matched at least 1 time (equivalent to "#(1,)").

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: A pattern notation "\N{reference}", where reference denotes a one-character-length template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter, matches the character in the referenced value or template.
requirements.original: A notation of the form "\N{reference}", where reference is denoting a one-character-length template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter, matches the character in the referenced value or template.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the reference in \N{reference} cannot be resolved
requirements.canonical: If the reference in a "\N{reference}" pattern notation cannot be resolved, the TTCN-3 tool SHALL generate an error.
requirements.original: If the reference cannot be resolved or if the referenced symbol is anything else than a template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter containing a character string of length 1, an error shall be generated.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.condition: the referenced symbol is not a one-character-length template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter
requirements.canonical: The reference in a "\N{reference}" pattern notation SHALL NOT denote anything other than a template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter containing a character string of length 1; otherwise an error SHALL be generated.
requirements.original: If the reference cannot be resolved or if the referenced symbol is anything else than a template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter containing a character string of length 1, an error shall be generated.

ambiguity.issue: Read together with "\N{typereference}" (next sentence), a reference to a charstring or universal charstring type is also allowed; this sentence lists only value-like symbols. The canonical text assumes the type form is an exception handled by B.1.5.4-s003.
readings: A "\N{...}" reference to anything other than a one-character template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter, including a charstring type reference, SHALL cause an error.
A "\N{...}" reference that is neither a one-character template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter nor a charstring or universal charstring type reference SHALL cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: A pattern notation "\N{typereference}", where typereference references a charstring or universal charstring type, matches any character of the character set denoted by the referenced type.
requirements.original: A notation of the form "\N{typereference}", where "typereference" is a reference to a charstring or universal `charstring` type, matches any character of the character set denoted by the referenced type.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: A referenced character set that is not a subset of the values allowed by the type of the template or template field in which the pattern is used IS NOT an error.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Cases when the referenced set of characters is not a subset of values allowed by the type definition of the template or template field for which the character pattern is used, are not be treated as an error (but e.g. matching never can occur if the two sets do not overlap).

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: A "\N{...}" pattern whose referenced character set does not overlap with the values allowed by the type of the template or template field CANNOT match any value.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Cases when the referenced set of characters is not a subset of values allowed by the type definition of the template or template field for which the character pattern is used, are not be treated as an error (but e.g. matching never can occur if the two sets do not overlap).

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: The pattern notation "\N{charstring}" IS equivalent to "?" when applied to a template or template field of charstring type.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: \N{charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of charstring type and \N{universal charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of universal charstring type (but causes an error if applied to a template or template field of charstring type).

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: The pattern notation "\N{universal charstring}" IS equivalent to "?" when applied to a template or template field of universal charstring type.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: \N{charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of charstring type and \N{universal charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of universal charstring type (but causes an error if applied to a template or template field of charstring type).

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: The pattern notation "\N{universal charstring}" SHALL NOT be applied to a template or template field of charstring type; doing so causes an error.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: \N{charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of charstring type and \N{universal charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of universal charstring type (but causes an error if applied to a template or template field of charstring type).

ambiguity.issue: This contradicts NOTE 1 (B.1.5.4-s004), which says a referenced character set that is not a subset of the template type is not an error, and B.1.5.5, which allows universal charstring type references in charstring patterns only if all characters have corresponding charstring characters. The canonical text follows NOTE 2 literally.
readings: Applying "\N{universal charstring}" to a charstring template SHALL cause an error.
Applying "\N{universal charstring}" to a charstring template IS NOT an error (NOTE 1); it only matches the characters that also exist in charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:type-compatibility
requirements.canonical: A referenced type, template, constant, variable or module parameter of type charstring MAY be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of universal charstring type.
requirements.original: For the purpose of referenced patterns (see clause 27.9) and references character sets (see clause B.1.5.3) specific type compatibility rules apply: a referenced type, template, constant, variable or module parameter of the type charstring always can be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of universal charstring type; a referenced type, template or value of the type universal charstring can be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of charstring type if all characters used in the referenced template or value and the character set allowed by the referenced type has their corresponding characters in the charstring type (see definition of corresponding characters in clause 6.3.1).

ambiguity.issue: "references character sets (see clause B.1.5.3)" refers to the referenced character sets of clause B.1.5.4; clause B.1.5.3 is "Match expression n times". Formal parameters, allowed as references in B.1.5.4, are not listed.

requirements.subject: ent:type-compatibility
requirements.condition: all referenced characters have corresponding characters in the charstring type
requirements.canonical: A referenced type, template or value of type universal charstring MAY be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of charstring type only if all characters used in the referenced template or value, and all characters of the character set allowed by the referenced type, have corresponding characters in the charstring type.
requirements.original: For the purpose of referenced patterns (see clause 27.9) and references character sets (see clause B.1.5.3) specific type compatibility rules apply: a referenced type, template, constant, variable or module parameter of the type charstring always can be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of universal charstring type; a referenced type, template or value of the type universal charstring can be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of charstring type if all characters used in the referenced template or value and the character set allowed by the referenced type has their corresponding characters in the charstring type (see definition of corresponding characters in clause 6.3.1).

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the check is on the actual characters used (value/template) or on the whole character set of the referenced type, and whether it is a compile-time or runtime check for variables and module parameters. "value" is used where the first half lists "constant, variable or module parameter". The canonical text requires both conditions.
readings: A universal charstring reference MAY be used in a charstring pattern if the characters actually used in the referenced value or template have corresponding charstring characters.
A universal charstring type reference MAY be used in a charstring pattern only if every character of the subtype character set has a corresponding charstring character.

requirements.subject: ent:nocase-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nocase` modifier IS placed directly after the `pattern` keyword.
requirements.original: When the "@nocase" modifier is used after the pattern keyword, the matching is evaluated in a case insensitive way, i.e. at positions, where without the "@nocase" modifier a small letter alphabetical character would be matched, with the "@nocase" modifier also capital letter counterpart - but only that - shall be accepted.

requirements.subject: ent:nocase-modifier
requirements.condition: the `@nocase` modifier is used after the `pattern` keyword
requirements.canonical: When the `@nocase` modifier is used, a pattern SHALL also accept the capital letter counterpart at every position where it would match a small letter alphabetical character without the modifier.
requirements.original: When the "@nocase" modifier is used after the pattern keyword, the matching is evaluated in a case insensitive way, i.e. at positions, where without the "@nocase" modifier a small letter alphabetical character would be matched, with the "@nocase" modifier also capital letter counterpart - but only that - shall be accepted.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence only describes small letters additionally accepting their capital counterparts, while it also says matching is "case insensitive". It is unclear whether a capital letter in the pattern also accepts its small letter counterpart.
readings: With `@nocase`, a pattern SHALL accept both the small and the capital counterpart of every alphabetical character in either direction.
With `@nocase`, a pattern SHALL additionally accept only the capital counterpart of small letters; capital letters in the pattern do not match small letters.

requirements.original: When the "@nocase" modifier is used after the pattern keyword, the matching is evaluated in a case insensitive way, i.e. at positions, where without the "@nocase" modifier a small letter alphabetical character would be matched, with the "@nocase" modifier also capital letter counterpart - but only that - shall be accepted.

requirements.subject: ent:nocase-modifier
requirements.condition: the `@nocase` modifier is used
requirements.canonical: When the `@nocase` modifier is used, a pattern matching the character đ (latin small letter d with stroke) SHALL also accept Đ (latin capital letter d with stroke).
requirements.original: For example, at positions where the pattern matches the character đ (latin small letter d with stroke), also its counterpart Đ (latin capital letter d with stroke) shall be accepted, but the similarly looking graphical characters Ð (latin capital letter eth) and Ɖ (latin capital letter african d) shall not.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-pattern
requirements.canonical: The case sensitivity property of a referenced pattern IS NOT inherited by the referencing pattern.
requirements.original: When referencing a pattern from inside another pattern (see clause 27.9), the case sensitivity property of the referenced pattern is not inherited.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-pattern
requirements.canonical: After dereferencing, possibly recursively, only the resulting string part of a referenced pattern IS inserted into the referencing pattern.
requirements.original: I.e. - after dereferencing, possibly recursively - only the resulting string part of the referenced pattern is inserted into the referencing pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern
requirements.canonical: A pattern containing references IS evaluated as a whole according to the case sensitivity of the referencing pattern.
requirements.original: The whole resulting pattern is always evaluated according to the casesensitivity of the referencing pattern.
